data.description:
## Context / Problem
Bug `misogynic-scheelite-solitaire` (ac3b-c6cd-8076-4a98, `1fce28eaf9b`) attaches `coverage.build_drift` (build and pinned SHAs, distance, and the remedy: update the checkout and run `make install`) to a gate verdict whose model never ran. Only the JSON output shows it, and the stderr degrade line points at the wrong cause.

Reproduced 2026-11-13 in a throwaway clone: running build `aa1681bb531`, attested config 2 commits ahead naming a Bedrock model id that does not exist, `rebar review-plan <id> --ref <sha>`:
- `--output=json`: verdict INDETERMINATE, `coverage.llm_ran=false`, `coverage.build_drift.remedy` = "this rebar build (aa1681bb5) is 2 commit(s) behind the config this gate read (37d8a50ab); update the checkout … and run `make install`, then re-run the gate". Correct.
- `--output=text` (the default an operator reads): only `PLAN REVIEW: INDETERMINATE`, the counts line and the source line. There is no build-drift line and no remedy.
- stderr: `llm-degrade: CHANGE_SETTINGS — The request exceeded a configured bound (tokens/steps/timeout) — adjust it and retry.` The provider said `The provided model identifier is invalid` (400 ValidationException). `failure.py` maps every malformed/invalid 400 to `CHANGE_SETTINGS`, and `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` describes only the bound case, so it sends the operator to tokens/steps/timeout.

## Approach
1. In the review-plan text renderer, when `coverage.build_drift` is present, print one `build drift:` line carrying its `remedy`, and for a model-never-ran verdict print the `llm_error` provider message (truncated) so the text report names the cause.
2. Reword `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` to cover what the class actually holds: a request the provider rejected because of a setting (model id, a token/step/timeout bound, or another request parameter); check the configured model and bounds. The classification itself does not change.
No new config key, env var or flag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A text-mode review-plan verdict whose `coverage` holds `build_drift` prints a line containing the remedy and `make install`; proved by a unit test on the renderer.
- [ ] A text-mode model-never-ran verdict prints the provider's error message.
- [ ] `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES["CHANGE_SETTINGS"]` mentions the model id as well as the bounds, and existing classification tests pass: `pytest tests/unit/test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py`.

## Testing
Add RED renderer tests (text output with and without `build_drift`) next to the existing review-plan text-output tests, and a message test. Run them, `make verify`, and re-run the throwaway-clone reproduction in text mode.
data.title: Degraded review-plan text report hides the build-skew remedy and misnames an invalid-request 400
